question: Which of the following is the first planned industrial city in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jamshedpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jamshedpur**, located in the state of Jharkhand, is the first planned industrial city in India.
 
• It was established by the visionary industrialist **Jamsetji Tata** in 1919 to serve as a hub for the Tata Steel Company.
 
• The city was designed by architect **Frederick Litchfield**, with well-planned infrastructure for industrial and residential areas.
 
• Jamshedpur is often referred to as **“Steel City”** or **“Tata Nagar”** due to its association with Tata Steel, one of the largest steel producers in India.
 
• The city is a pioneer in urban planning in India, featuring wide roads, efficient drainage systems, and designated industrial zones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial City Concept:**

 
 
• An industrial city is a planned urban area designed to cater to manufacturing and industrial activities.
 
• It includes infrastructure like factories, warehouses, and residential areas for workers.
 
 
 
• **Jamsetji Tata:**
 
 
• The founder of the Tata Group, he envisioned Jamshedpur as an industrial hub for India's economic growth.
 
• He laid the foundation for Tata Steel, Asia’s first integrated steel plant.
 
 
 
• **Urban Planning in Jamshedpur:**
 
 
• The city has a unique layout with separate zones for industries, housing, and recreational areas.
 
• It is managed by the Tata Steel Utilities and Infrastructure Services Limited (formerly JUSCO).
 
 
 
• **Significance of Jamshedpur:**
 
 
• The city is a center for steel production, contributing significantly to India's industrial output.
 
• It has won awards for cleanliness and urban management, making it a model for other industrial towns.
